bearer.description: The per-launch token the app hands the sidecar on stdin.

provider.description: Override the global provider for this feature.

model.description: Override the resolved model for this feature.

error.description: What went wrong, as a sentence.

detail.description: The raw message behind it, for the log and a help tag (a `/v2` route's failure); never the visible line.

ApiError.description: What a route answers when it cannot do what was asked (a 400).

source.description: `keychain`: handed over by the Mac app from the macOS Keychain.

sourceText.description: Where the key comes from, in words ("From the Keychain"); null when there is no key.

ApiKeyStatus.description: The active provider's key state, with where keys are kept (`GET /api/settings`).

upstreamUrl.description: The project this one began as a fork of; shown as credit, never used as a feed.

unknown.description: What is not known, as sentences. An empty list means nothing is missing, never "not checked".

wouldChange.description: What would change the reading, as sentences.

called.description: How the reading is called, in the GM's words: `certainty` said plainly ("A fact from the export"), which the app shows under "How it's called" (a code this build does not know still has its words).

stamp.description: The D-041 stamp shown in the evidence view (a breakdown, where a method word may help).

Basis.description: Why a claim says what it says (D-018, D-023, D-031, D-044: show the basis).

BasisLine.description: One line of a claim's evidence: what was read and what it said.

specialist.description: The specialist, in words ("Data status", "Player Value").

asOf.description: When the evidence was read (an import's time, ISO 8601), or null when it has not been.

gameDate.description: The game date the evidence reflects, as the export wrote it, or null.

sample.description: How much evidence there is, in words ("30 games"), when that matters.

BasisSource.description: Who answered: the department and its specialist, and how current the evidence is.

isHuman.description: The save's human runs the club; null when the export does not say.

logo.description: Where to fetch the logo (`/api/logo/:teamId?v=…`), or null when the save holds none.

record.description: Wins and losses ("45–38"), or the sentence for a record the export does not have.

theme.description: The theme the club wears in the Mac app (D-062): its own colours unless another pack was chosen for it, every appearance resolved and checked. `palette` stays for the React app's colours.

CatalogClub.description: A major-league club: its palette, where its logo is, and its record as the export has it.

views.description: Its views in the sidebar's order (SWIFTUI_REBUILD.md section 3.5).

head.description: The person in the department's seat; null when the save names nobody there or the department has no one seat.

preparedBy.description: The masthead line ("Prepared by Jeff Banister, bench coach"), or what the save does not say.

CatalogPhrases.description: Sentences the app shows in more than one place: for a served value that is missing and no line of its own says why, and the legends under the design's graphics (the app keeps only their symbols).

id.description: The view's id inside its department (`fortyManOptions`), the Mac app's route.

CatalogView.description: One view of a department, as the sidebar lists it.

claimRef.description: A claim elsewhere in the payload that explains this cell.

Cell.description: One cell of a served table: what it shows, and its tone and help tag when it has them.

Certainty.description: How a claim's number or line is called (D-041): `calibrated` (fitted on the save's own history), `provisional` (a model parameter that ought to be fitted and has not been), `policy` (a line chosen and stated, never fitted), `unknown` (the basis cannot say), and `fact`: an objective fact read from the export or the save (a record, a date, how many days one source is behind another), which no fitted number and no chosen line decided. Section 4.1 listed the first four; `fact` was added at N4 so a plain fact is never stamped as policy.

hint.description: The help tag: one line, at most about 75 characters.

Claim.description: One visible line, in the GM's voice, with its basis.

ClaimTrail.description: The evidence trail behind an item, fetched on demand (`GET /api/v2/claims/:key`): too slow to put in a summary (an MLB need's staff recommendation takes seconds on a real save), so the inspector asks for it when the GM opens the item.

team.description: The club's plate (its primary colour, adjusted until its text reads) and the text on it.

ClubPalette.description: A club's palette in one mode, as the Mac app is served it: every token as `#rrggbb`.

ClubPalettes.description: A club's palette in both modes.

why.description: Why the import did not start; null when it did.

ConfigAccepted.description: What `POST /api/config` answers: the save is chosen, and whether its import began. A save whose export folder is not there yet is chosen all the same, and `why` says what to do in a sentence.

ConfigRequest.description: The save to use (`POST /api/config`): its CSV export folder and its name.

humanClubs.description: How many clubs the save's human manages (automatic follows the first, by team id).

note.description: When automatic had to pick among several human clubs, which one it follows and why, in a sentence; else null.

CurrentOrganization.description: The club the app is about when nothing names one: the configured organization, else the one the save's human manages; null when neither is known. A configured id is taken as configured even when the club list no longer has it (the server's rule for every view), so a client shows that club as not found rather than quietly switching clubs.

lgPath.description: Diagnostic: where the `.lg` was found. Not something the user has to supply.

simulatedThrough.description: Last simulated in-game date (ISO), from the save itself.

currentDate.description: `leagues.current_date` of the imported export (ISO): the day about to be played.

simulatedThrough.description: The last day the imported data reflects.

ratingMode.description: Which kind of ratings the export carries, as the import read OOTP's export settings; null for an import from before N3.5.

leftOut.description: Files the import left out (older than the rest of the export, or unreadable), and what their tables hold.

import.description: What the imported export carries and what its import left out (N3.5, D-061).

DataStatusFact.description: One fact of the data status: what it is ("Game date") and its value ("May 15, 2026"), or why it is missing.

DataStatusRow.description: One line of the data status: a source ("League data") and its state ("Behind by 2 days").

level.description: The freshness model's level, for the symbol beside the headline (`current`, `partial`, `stale`, `unavailable`).

headline.description: The headline, with the reasons and what would change it in its basis.

subtitle.description: The window's subtitle, short enough for the title bar: the game date and a word or two ("May 15, 2026 · Log behind").

subtitleHint.description: The subtitle in full, for its help tag: the game date and the headline ("May 15, 2026 · Transactions 2 days behind").

sources.description: League data, transactions, the OOTP save and roster evidence.

facts.description: Dates and places, every one present: a missing value says why.

action.description: What to do about it, when there is something to do.

leftOut.description: Files the last import left out, in a sentence, each file and why in its basis; null when none was (N3.5).

top.description: The first things it is watching (at most three): the desk already shows what it has to decide.

toDecide.description: How many items it has to decide and to watch; null when it could not be read or has no report yet.

open.description: Opens the department's report; null when it has none yet.

DepartmentCard.description: A department's compact card on the Morning Report.

role.description: The seat, as the save's staff page names it ("Bench Coach", "Team Doctor").

DepartmentHead.description: Who heads a department, as the save's staff has it.

importStamp.description: The import the report was built from (the last import's finish time), or null when the server has none on record.

reportStamp.description: The build it comes from: moves whenever the server builds the Front Office again (a new import, a settings change, a calibration).

preparedBy.description: "Prepared by Jeff Banister, bench coach", or its staff when the save names nobody.

asOf.description: "Through May 16, 2040": the game date the evidence reflects, or why it is not known.

summary.description: One sentence assembled from its items.

changes.description: What changed since the last export; null until Pennant keeps each import's reports (N7), never an empty list.

memo.description: The staff memo; null until the AI pass writes one.

DepartmentReport.description: A department's report, one anatomy for all (SWIFTUI_REBUILD.md section 3.5).

DeptId.description: A department of the club, as the Mac app's sidebar has them (SWIFTUI_REBUILD.md section 3.5). An open enum in the spec: a newer server may name a department an older app does not know.

order.description: How the desk is ordered and what it shows, in words, with the full rule in its help tag.

more.description: Each department with more to decide than the desk shows, and how many more.

empty.description: "Nothing to decide from the departments reporting" when every department was read and none raised anything; null otherwise.

incomplete.description: Which departments could not be read, so the desk may be missing items; null when every one was.

Desk.description: The desk: the items to decide from every department (a stated share of each), in a stated order.

DeskMore.description: A department's items to decide beyond the desk's stated share, and where they are.

DeskSeverity.description: The desk's common scale, most urgent first.

ExportPendingEvent.description: OOTP has written a fresh export the server has not imported yet.

key.description: The item's key within an import: its department, its kind and its subject (`majorLeague:need:mlb:il_return_crunch:412`). The same problem keeps the same key from one build to the next of the same import.

raisedBy.description: Who raised it: the department's head as the save names him ("Raised by Jeff Banister, bench coach"), or its staff.

severity.description: The department's own severity on the desk's scale, with its philosophy and season weighed (never above what it said).

neutralSeverity.description: What the department states with no philosophy and no season to weigh: the plain reading, and what the desk goes by (whether it is to decide or to watch, and its order; D-060). The same as `severity` when nothing shaded it.

urgency.description: The plain severity in words ("Urgent", "Needs attention", "Noted"), with the line that placed it and any lean in its basis.

headline.description: What it is, in one line, with the department's evidence as its basis.

detail.description: A second line when there is one (who is out, where he plays); null when the headline says it all.

due.description: The days left on a running clock ("3 days left"), or null when nothing is counting down.

dueInDays.description: The same, as a number for ordering; null when there is no clock or its days are not exported.

evidence.description: The key of the evidence trail `GET /api/v2/claims/:key` serves for it; null when it has none beyond its basis.

count.description: How many of the department's own items this row stands for: 1, or more when the grouping rule put several in one row.

FoItem.description: One thing a department raised for the GM.

through.description: Simulated-through date on the common basis, ISO.
Simulated-through date on the common basis, ISO.

headline.description: One line, e.g. "Partial — transaction log 1 day behind".

action.description: What the user should do about it, when there is something to do.

club.description: The club's name, or null when the export does not have it.

importStamp.description: The import it was built from; the Mac app's stores key on the same stamp.

reportStamp.description: The build it comes from (`DepartmentReport.reportStamp`); `/api/status` and the `front-office-updated` event serve the current one.

FrontOfficeSummary.description: The Morning Report's desk and department cards (`GET /api/v2/front-office/:org`).

FrontOfficeUpdatedEvent.description: The server built a club's Front Office again and keeps it (a new import, a settings change, a calibration): its new `reportStamp`. The Mac app's Front Office store reloads on it (a cached read).

GameDate.description: An in-game date as the server serves it. A string, never a date type: OOTP writes dates unpadded (`2026-5-9`), and although the fields that pass through `parseGameDate` are padded, a client compares or orders game dates only as the server does (D-056). The contract (`contract/openapi.json`) names it `GameDate`, with no format.

GameDateText.description: A game date as served (unpadded, as OOTP writes it, or null) and as the app shows it.

display.description: The term as a column shows it ("OPS+", "GB").

text.description: What it means, in sentences: the help the app shows for the column.

GlossaryEntry.description: A term and what it means (a column label and its explanation).

HelloEvent.description: The first event on every stream: the `/api/status` snapshot, so nothing is missed between loading and listening.

ImportAccepted.description: What `POST /api/import` answers: the import has started; its progress and result arrive on `/api/status` and the event stream.

error.description: The raw error, for the log; `note` says it in words.

note.description: Why the import did not finish, in a sentence; null when it did.

kind.description: What happened: `failed` (it stopped on an error), `interrupted` (the server stopped partway), `exportMissing`.

detail.description: The raw message behind it, for the log and a help tag; never the visible line.

ImportNote.description: Why an import is not where the GM expects it, in a sentence, with the raw message kept for the log.

table.description: The table being written, as OOTP names the file.

fileIndex.description: 1-based, so it reads as "12 of 70" without arithmetic.

rows.description: Rows written so far, across every table.

phase.description: `waiting` (N3.5): OOTP is still writing the export, and the import waits for it to finish.

ImportProgress.description: Where the import has got to, for a page that would rather not look frozen: the step, and the step in words.

csvDir.description: The export folder this import read (N3.5).

exportFingerprint.description: The export's fingerprint (its files' names, sizes and times), to tell a new export from this one (N3.5).

exportWrittenAt.description: When OOTP wrote the newest file of the export this import read (N3.5).

leftOut.description: Files of the export the import left out, each with why and what the database holds for its table (N3.5).

leftOutNote.description: The files left out, in a sentence for the GM; null when none was (N3.5).

ratingMode.description: Which kind of ratings the export carries, from OOTP's export settings, read at this import (N3.5, D-061).

durationMs.description: How long the import took, in milliseconds, from the build's start to the swap (N3.5).

ImportResult.description: What an import did: its tables and rows, when it ran, the export it read, what it left out, and the kind of ratings.

phase.description: What the import is doing ("Reading the export").

table.description: The table being written, named for a person ("Standings"); its OOTP file name stays in `table`.

display.description: The line a progress bar shows ("Writing standings · 12 of 70").

ImportWords.description: An import step in words (`server/presentation/importWords.ts`), for a window that shows it.

Integer.description: A whole number: an id, a count, a season, a number of days. The spec says `type: integer`, so the Mac app reads an `Int`, not a `Double`. A true decimal (a rate, a slider, dollars) stays `number`. Named `Integer`, never `Int`, which the Swift generator would rename.

JobEvent.description: A background job (storylines, the briefing) changed state for one club.

source.description: `keychain`: handed over by the Mac app from the macOS Keychain.

sourceText.description: Where the key comes from, in words ("From the Keychain"); null when there is no key.

Lean.description: The organization's philosophy leaning on a reading (D-052's lens): the neutral reading beside the reasons for the lean. A claim with no lean says so with `null`; an absent lean is never read as "neutral".

reason.description: `stale`: older than the rest of the export (not rewritten); `unreadable`: it could not be parsed.

kept.description: Whether the database keeps the previous import's rows for this table (stale files only, same export folder).

keptFrom.description: When the kept rows were imported; null when nothing is kept.

LeftOutFile.description: A file the import left out (N3.5).

lastTransactionDate.description: The newest date on any transaction row.

activityThrough.description: The newest date on any day-stamped table in the database.

coveredThrough.description: How far the database has demonstrably been written. Days with no transactions (off-season, an off-day) leave `lastTransactionDate` behind without the log being behind, so this takes the newest of everything.

found.description: The live transaction database exists in the save's temp folder.

Ok.description: A request the server accepted, with nothing more to say.

Org.description: A major-league club as `GET /api/orgs` lists it.

mode.description: V1 uses manual. Staff and hybrid exist now so V2 can be introduced without changing the persisted shape.

manual.description: User-selected values. Always available as a fallback.

overrides.description: In hybrid mode these dimensions stay user-controlled while the others may come from staff.

Place.description: A league place, stated (D-057): `rank` among `of` clubs that have the figure, `tiedWith` the number of other clubs on the same figure, and, for a Player Value place, `overlap`: how many clubs' ranges overlap this one.

PlaceLegend.description: The legend under "How we win and lose": what each mark on a place strip means.

ProviderChoice.description: A provider on offer, with the model it would use (`GET /api/settings/providers`).

ProviderId.description:
Four ways to reach a model, behind one shape.

The app was written against Anthropic and every feature still works best there — the chat's tool loop and prompt caching are Anthropic's shapes, and this is where they stay. What this adds is a choice for anyone who already pays for a key somewhere else, which is most of the reason people asked.

Only the parts that genuinely differ are adapted. A system prompt is a separate argument at Anthropic, the first message at OpenAI, and its own field at Google; a refusal is a stop reason, a field on the message, and a finish reason respectively. Those are normalised here so the four call sites upstream never learn which provider answered.

ProviderInfo.description: One AI service the app can talk to, as the Settings screen lists it.

ProvidersResponse.description: What `GET /api/settings/providers` serves: the providers on offer and every provider's key state.

additionalScouted.description: "Additional complete scouted ratings" (OOTP's option), when the file says; null when it does not.

source.description: Where the mode came from: the save's export settings, or why they could not be read.

reason.description: Why the mode is unknown, in a sentence; null when it is known.

RatingModeRecord.description: The export's rating mode as the import recorded it, with how it was read.

problem.description: The first thing wrong, as the GM reads it.

details.description: Everything wrong with it, one sentence each, for whoever fixes the file.

RefusedThemePack.description: A pack in the data folder that was refused, and why, in a sentence (the details in its help tag).

ReportChange.description: What changed since the last export (N7 fills it).

empty.description: The line shown when there are no items ("Nothing to decide"); null when there are items or nothing could be read.

ReportSection.description: "To decide" or "Watching": a titled list of items, and what it says when it is empty.

ReportStatus.description: A department's report is ready, could not be read this time, or has nothing to report yet.

ReportUnknowns.description: "What we can't see": the department's unknowns, as short sentences.

ResolveFolderRequest.description: The folder the user picked or typed (`POST /api/resolve-folder`).

saves.description: Saves found inside the chosen folder, when it holds several.

range.description: The range bar and its hatching.

need.description: The ring and the word for a need.

RosterLegend.description: The legend under the roster diagram: what each mark on a plate means, and what the pointer does.

SaveList.description: The saves found in the usual places (`GET /api/saves`).

SaveSourceRequest.description: The `<save>.lg` folder named by hand (`POST /api/save-source`); empty or null returns to automatic.

SaveSourceResult.description: What `POST /api/save-source` answers once the save folder is set or cleared.

SearchLocation.description: One place the server looks for saves: a human label, the folder, and whether it exists here.

SearchLocations.description: Where `GET /api/search-locations` looked for saves, so the user can see why auto-detection came up empty.

low.description: The low end of the range, when the value is a range (the most likely value is `n`).

high.description: The high end of the range; never "the whole" of anything (a share of a whole is `whole`).

whole.description: The whole this value is a count of, when it is a real "x of y" ("26 of 26" on the active roster: `n` 26, `whole` 26). Only a value served with it is drawn as a share (a ring or a bar); the app never infers a whole from a range.

display.description: The value as the app shows it ("4.8 runs a game", "Not known yet").

ServedValue.description: A number a claim shows, with its range when it has one. `n` null is a value the evidence cannot give; `display` always says something (the sentence for a missing value, never a zero or a dash).

ServerEvent.description:
What the server tells a connected app as it happens, over `GET /api/v2/events` (server-sent events, D-055).

The React app polls `/api/status` every few seconds; the Mac app listens here instead. Every event is a fact the server already holds (the same fields `/api/status` and the job routes serve), pushed when it changes. An event is a nudge to re-read, never a second source of truth: a client that missed one reads `/api/status`, and the stream opens with a `hello` carrying that snapshot so nothing is missed between loading and listening.

The names are the contract's (N2 describes them in `contract/openapi.json`); a client ignores a name it does not know, so new events can be added without breaking an older app.

app.description: Product name and version, from package.json (see appInfo.ts).

importProgress.description: Where a running import has got to; null when nothing is importing.

importInterruptedSince.description: Set when an import stopped partway (the server was stopped or crashed); cleared by the next completed import.

importNote.description: Why the import is not where it should be, in a sentence (a failure, an interruption, a missing export); null when it is.

exportPending.description: Set when OOTP has written a fresh export the app has not imported yet.

logoToken.description: Changes with the save, and rides along on every logo URL.

ratingScaleMax.description: The top of the rating scale the save shows ratings on.

reportStamp.description: The stamp of the Front Office's current build for the club the app follows (`FrontOfficeSummary.reportStamp`), or null before one is kept. It moves whenever the server builds the Front Office again; the Mac app reloads on it.

ServerStatus.description: What `/api/status` serves, and the snapshot `/api/v2/events` opens with (described in `contract/openapi.json`).

autoImport.description: Watch the save's export folder for a new export (the React label: "Watch for new exports").

importAutomatically.description: Import a new export in the background as soon as OOTP has finished writing it (N3.5, the owner's decision 1, 2026-09-26: on by default). Needs `autoImport` (the watch); off, a new export is only offered, as before.

theme.description: 'system' follows the OS setting and changes with it.

model.description: Model id used by every AI feature. See models.ts for the picker's list.

provider.description: Which service the AI features talk to. Anthropic unless changed — it is what the app was built against and the only one the chat's tool loop and prompt caching are native to.

models.description: The model chosen for each provider, remembered separately. Switching provider would otherwise leave a model id the new one has never heard of.

aiFeatures.description:
Optional provider/model overrides for individual AI workloads.

Missing entries inherit the global provider and that provider's selected model, preserving the behaviour of existing settings files.

roundRatingsToFive.description: Write overall and potential in fives, the way scouts talk. Display only — sorting and every calculation keep the exact grade.

showUnavailablePitchers.description:
Keep pitchers on the injured list in the bullpen table.

Off unless asked for. That page answers one question — who can throw tonight — and a man six weeks from a rehab start is not an answer to it. Nothing vanishes quietly: the heading says how many are being held back and hands them over in a click.

autoGenerateAfterImport.description:
Write the storylines and the briefing by themselves after each import.

Off unless asked for. Both cost money on someone else's API key, and a setting that quietly spends it would be a poor default however convenient.

nextSeasonBudget.description:
What you expect the owner to hand you next season, per club, in dollars.

OOTP does not publish a future budget — it is not set until the offseason — so future headroom had to assume this year's holds flat. On a club whose budget swings, that is the wrong number to plan against, and you are the one who knows which way the owner leans. Absent an entry, flat it stays.

organizationPhilosophies.description: Organizational philosophy is saved per club. The string key is the OOTP organization/team id so different clubs and saves may think differently.

themePacks.description: The theme pack each club wears in the Mac app (D-062), by team id; a club left out wears its own colours. Written only by `POST /api/v2/theme-packs/:org` (`themePackStore.ts`); the React app ignores it.

Settings.description:
User preferences, plus the Anthropic API key.

The key is a real secret, so it is never written in plain text when we can avoid it: the desktop app hands us Electron's safeStorage, which encrypts against the OS keychain (Keychain on macOS, DPAPI on Windows). Running from source in a browser there is no keychain available, so the key falls back to a 0600 file and the UI says so plainly rather than implying it is protected.

organization.description: The club the app is about: the configured organization, else the human-managed one (`viewingOrganization.ts`).

SettingsSaved.description: What `POST /api/settings` answers: the preferences as saved.

autoImport.description: Watch the save's export folder for a new export (the React label: "Watch for new exports").

importAutomatically.description: Import a new export in the background as soon as OOTP has finished writing it (N3.5, the owner's decision 1, 2026-09-26: on by default). Needs `autoImport` (the watch); off, a new export is only offered, as before.

roundRatingsToFive.description: Write overall and potential in fives, the way scouts talk. Display only — sorting and every calculation keep the exact grade.

showUnavailablePitchers.description:
Keep pitchers on the injured list in the bullpen table.

Off unless asked for. That page answers one question — who can throw tonight — and a man six weeks from a rehab start is not an answer to it. Nothing vanishes quietly: the heading says how many are being held back and hands them over in a click.

autoGenerateAfterImport.description:
Write the storylines and the briefing by themselves after each import.

Off unless asked for. Both cost money on someone else's API key, and a setting that quietly spends it would be a poor default however convenient.

theme.description: 'system' follows the OS setting and changes with it.

provider.description: Which service the AI features talk to. Anthropic unless changed — it is what the app was built against and the only one the chat's tool loop and prompt caching are native to.

model.description: Model id used by every AI feature. See models.ts for the picker's list.

models.description: The model chosen for each provider, remembered separately. Switching provider would otherwise leave a model id the new one has never heard of.

aiFeatures.description:
Optional provider/model overrides for individual AI workloads.

Missing entries inherit the global provider and that provider's selected model, preserving the behaviour of existing settings files.

SettingsUpdate.description:
What `POST /api/settings` takes: the preferences to change. A field left out keeps its value, and a value the handler cannot use is ignored. (Philosophy and next season's budget have routes of their own.)

`clubChoice: 'automatic'` forgets the chosen club, so the app follows the club the save's human manages (`viewingOrganization.ts`). It is the Mac app's way back to automatic: its generated client never sends an explicit null, so it cannot clear `defaultOrgId` by sending one (SWIFTUI_REBUILD.md section 4.3). It wins over a `defaultOrgId` sent beside it.

shmPresent.description: Whether the source had a `-shm` file. It is never copied.

sourceModified.description: Modification times of the source files when copied.

StaffMemo.description: A staff member's memo (the later AI pass fills it; never part of a decision, D-001).

key.description: The key of the stat in a served stat block.

format.description: How a value is written: `int`, `avg3` (.312), `dec1`, `dec2`, `pct` (a share), `plus` (100 is league average).

lowerIsBetter.description: Lower is better (an ERA, a strikeout rate for a hitter).

StatEntry.description: One statistic the app can show.

view.description: A view's id inside its department (`fortyManOptions`).

key.description: A decision's key inside its department.

Target.description: Where a claim or a row leads: a department, one of its views, a player, a club or a decision. Flat, with the fields its kind needs, so the app reads one shape.

ThemeChoice.description: What `POST /api/v2/theme-packs/:org` takes: the pack the club should wear (`club-colors` for its own colours).

active.description: The pack the club wears now (`club-colors` unless another was chosen and is still installed and sound).

refused.description: Packs in the data folder that were refused.

unavailable.description: A chosen pack that is no longer installed or no longer passes, so the club wears its own colours; null when none.

folder.description: Where packs go, for the GM to find: the data folder's `theme-packs` folder.

ThemeChoices.description: The themes a club can wear (`GET /api/v2/theme-packs/:org`): its own colours first, then each installed pack that fits.

id.description: `club-colors` for the club's own colours; an installed pack's folder name.

name.description: The pack's name as its file gives it, or "Club colours" for the club's own.

version.description: The pack's own version, as its file gives it (the club's own colours: the format's).

teamId.description: The club the pack is made for; null when it is made for any club.

logo.description: Where to fetch the pack's logo, else the save's own logo for the club; null when there is neither.

art.description: Where to fetch the pack's masthead art; null when it has none.

ThemePack.description: A theme pack as served: checked, with every appearance's colours resolved.

ThemePackKind.description: Where a pack comes from: the club's own colours (derived from the save), or a pack installed in the data folder.

mastheadTop.description: The top of the masthead, under the toolbar, where macOS writes the window's title and subtitle in its own label colour: nearly white in light, nearly black in dark, so the title reads as it does on a plain window.

masthead.description: The masthead's colours, from its leading top to its trailing bottom (one to four), under its text.

mastheadText.description: The masthead's headline text (the view's title, the club, the record).

accent.description: The club's one accent, as a colour on the window's background (a link, a mark, a chart's own series).

tint.description: The tint of the one floating control a view may have.

card.description: The club card's fill in the sidebar, and its text.

ThemeTokens.description: The colours one appearance draws. Each colour that text sits on comes with its text, and every pair reads (4.5:1, or 7:1 for Increase Contrast): the server checks them before it serves a pack.

lightIncreasedContrast.description: Light with Increase Contrast on: every pair at 7:1.

ThemeVariants.description: A pack's colours for each appearance.

Tone.description: How a line reads at a glance. Colour is never the only signal: the app pairs a tone with a symbol and a word.

empty.description: What the section says when it has no claims; null when it has some.

TrailSection.description: One titled part of an evidence trail.

Unit.description: What a served number counts, so the app formats it (a share as a percentage, dollars as money).

UnknownServerEvent.description: An event this build of the contract does not name, sent by a newer server. The spec lists it last among `ServerEvent`'s shapes, so an older app decodes it (and ignores it) instead of failing the stream.
